findings.namedBuyers: No verified named hotel buyer identified. Two named venue-side referral contacts are Paul Gagnon, Director of Rental Events, and Natalie Ireland, Senior Manager, Events, both listed by TO Live. Their roles make them plausible introductions to the programme organiser or event logistics team (inference); neither is proven assigned to STOMP or authorised to contract accommodation. Use the historical STOMP@toronto.ca programme mailbox to request the current City lead.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced: Saturday, May 1, 2027, 1 p.m., Meridian Hall, Toronto, Ontario, Canada; doors 12:30 p.m. This is an activity date, not an article timestamp, and falls within the requested horizon. The City states: “More details about the 2027 Stomp Urban Dance Competition & Showcase to come soon.” No official 2028 edition located; do not extrapolate its date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: geographically plausible downtown lodging, but a weak demonstrated room-demand case. The City describes teams from across Toronto, so day attendance may dominate; this does not establish zero overnight demand. A 157-room Harbourfront hotel could accommodate a limited travelling team/chaperone group, visiting judges or production personnel only if such demand is confirmed. No evidence supports a 15–109-room block or any other block size. The 240-theatre ballroom is not an alternative to the incumbent performance theatre or the historically reported audience. City-hotel lodging is more relevant than a resort retreat; do not propose exclusive event housing or assume catering is operating.
findings.venueCommitments: The City explicitly names Meridian Hall for May 1, 2027. Address: 1 Front Street East, Toronto, Ontario M5E 1B2. It is in Toronto proper, downtown, not at MTCC or Exhibition Place and not a competing hotel. This is a public venue announcement; an executed venue contract was not inspected. No hotel commitment was located.
findings.historicalRotation: Documented Toronto history: Queen Elizabeth Theatre at Exhibition Place in 2010; Sony Centre for the Performing Arts in 2019; Meridian Hall in 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026, with 2027 announced there. Sony Centre was renamed Meridian Hall in September 2019: that name change is not a venue rotation. Evidence supports local venue continuity, not a rotating national destination-selection opportunity. The official 2027 page explicitly calls it annual; no assumption of uninterrupted editions is required.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific official housing bureau, host hotel, hotel list, room block or open hotel RFP was located; therefore there are no published block hotels to name. The 2027 City announcement says “More details about the 2027 Stomp Urban Dance Competition & Showcase to come soon”; this is not an accommodation-sourcing invitation. Historical performer guidelines direct programme queries to STOMP@toronto.ca and say “Pay by cheque payable to City of Toronto”; these establish a programme route, not hotel procurement authority. Independent family/team booking is a possibility only, not verified sourcing.
findings.organizationStructure: Municipal youth recreation event, not a membership association or a commercial touring STOMP production. City documentation identifies Parks, Forestry and Recreation as the programme originator; the 2023 event listing identifies presentation by the City division in partnership with TO Live. TO Live is the venue-side partner/operator, not an established accommodation buyer. No external PCO, DMC or housing agency identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Meridian Hall is the announced performance venue and has multiyear continuity. No incumbent accommodation hotels, hotel exclusivity, sold-out inventory, overflow requirement or displaced demand were found. The 2019 audience of approximately 2,150 and more than 250 performers are historical attendance figures, not room demand, not a 2027 forecast and not proof of overflow. Main limitation is unproven non-local travel rather than a documented competing hotel contract.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Send one qualification-first message to the historically published STOMP@toronto.ca mailbox, referencing the announced May 1, 2027 Meridian Hall edition. Ask for the current City programme lead, non-local participant/judge/crew numbers, overnight dates, who books/pays, and any incumbent accommodation agreement. If routing fails, seek an introduction through TO Live’s Paul Gagnon or Natalie Ireland. Offer a small, appropriately supervised lodging solution only after demand and purchasing access are established; otherwise retain as low-priority relationship development, not a qualified group-room opportunity.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The next announced edition is May 1, 2027; May 2, 2026 is historical. Performance-venue capture is not an open opportunity on current evidence. Accommodation accessibility remains unknown, not open and not committed elsewhere on the available evidence. Only exploratory lodging qualification is justified; do not assign speculative room revenue.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: cultivate the City programme relationship for any verified visiting-team, judge or production lodging associated with later editions. Annual recurrence is explicit, but no 2028 date, venue search, hotel tender or rotating-host process was found. Future competitive capture means a possible lodging relationship, not evidence that the show venue is contestable.
